title: a-probe-reads-the-tree-the-face-writes
owner: the librarian (the probe berths beside its code at cairn/devices/librarian/probes/; Law 6)
why: The lived symptom: the-tenure-loop's WATCHME was armed and sealed at PROVED on 2026-08-09, and on 2026-08-10 it can report nothing — not 'the loop is healthy', not 'the loop is decorative', nothing at all — because its census returns zero rows and its trigger needs >= 20 post-era crossings to fire. A watch that cannot bite is arming theatre: the voyage closed on a gate that checked the probe EXISTS at its declared path, which it does, while the thing it was built to observe went unobserved. This is the exact failure the WATCHME summons was inverted to prevent (node_classes/code-seam.json v2: 'optional to carry, MANDATORY TO SATISFY once carried') — the crossing was satisfied by a module that imports, not by an instrument that measures. It also has a second cost, which is how it surfaced: the probe is the template every later librarian probe copies, so a dead substrate propagates by imitation. revision-with-receipts was specified to copy this shape and had to be steered off it by hand.

proves_green.proof: a tooth beside the code asserting the probe's census against a seeded fixture returns the seeded rows — i.e. the instrument reads where the face writes. A hollow build passes 'the module imports'; it does not pass 'the census sees the rows the live face deposited', which is the tooth this ticket owes.
proves_green.feeds_back_to_origin_on_failure: a kick-back re-enters BUILDME on the-tenure-loop's probe, since the artifact under repair is that ticket's WATCHME (Laws 3 + 8).

falsifier.proves_red: Two ways this ticket is wrong. (1) MISAIMED: if 'commons' is the intended home of the librarian's live corpus and the defect is really at the writing end — shim.py:35 writing 'library' when it should write 'commons' — then the one-line fix belongs at the other end and this ticket points the wrong way. Discriminator: which tree does the librarian's charter name, and which one do the ratified library-fold and summary nodes sit in? (2) INSUFFICIENT: if after the fix the probe's survey function still returns zero rows against the live store, or its trigger arithmetic is still unreachable, then the tree constant was not the whole defect and the ticket closed on a symptom.
falsifier.horizon: at the fix plus one live crossing: the probe's survey function called directly against the live store must return a NON-ZERO row count, and its trigger must be evaluable against real arithmetic rather than an empty set. Re-check within one voyage — this is the instrument for a component under active build, so a stale answer here is expensive immediately.

priority: P1 — Not from a trouble, so it earns P1 on the charter's other clause: an issue on the LIVE SYSTEM NOW. The probe is armed and sealed on the running system today, and what it reports is a false green — silence that reads as 'nothing to see' when the instrument is pointed at an address nothing writes to. Law 9: a green that was never earned is worse than a red.
watchme: none, because the artifact under repair IS the watch. A watch on a watch has no independent instrument — the probe's own census returning non-zero against the live store is both the fix's proof and its ongoing observation, and it is already the horizon above. Resolvable referent: cairn/devices/librarian/probes/standing_moves_under_live_use.py, whose repaired census is the standing measure.
sorted_berth: none, because direct TICKET entry — see intent_berth. The finding stands measured in /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/survey-20260810T133527-4e19d02b69fc.json (absences[4]), which is the packet that produced it.
intent_berth: none, because this is a direct TICKET entry rather than a birthed intention — the three-entry-points ruling (2026-08-02) makes TICKET a door of its own, and a bug does not pass IDEA or INTENT. The resolvable referent for how it was found is the survey berth below.
chart_claim: validate-20260810T152430-b4118f721672 — chart chain complete with real content; verdict berthed at verdict-20260810T153340-cc36400fd97a
cast_by: direct TICKET entry — ruling 2026-08-02-three-entry-points-and-structural-refiled, recorded in CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json `entry`. Editing one line fixes it, which is that ruling's own test for bug-rather-than-structural.
intent: Point the tenure loop's armed WATCHME at the tree the live face actually writes, so the watch can fire. cairn/devices/librarian/probes/standing_moves_under_live_use.py line 44 sets _TREE = 'commons' and line 88 censuses only that tree; the librarian's live face constructs its session with tree='library' (cairn/devices/librarian/shim.py:35). The probe therefore surveys an address the running system never writes to. The fix is one constant; the ticket exists because a bug enters at a door, not at an edit.
measure: store.read('librarian_nodes', where="tree = 'commons'") = 0 rows on 2026-08-10. Full census 78 rows at survey time, tree distribution Counter({'library': 74, 'founding': 4}); after three live crossings the same day, 87 rows, still none in 'commons'. Probe source line 44 _TREE = 'commons'; line 88 reads WHERE tree = %s with that constant; _ENOUGH_CROSSINGS / _trigger requires >= 20 crossings, unreachable on an empty tree at any horizon.
known_adjacent_debt: NOT scoped into this ticket, recorded so the one-line fix is not mistaken for the whole truth: the librarian has three disagreeing default trees live at once — loop.py:189, chat.py:143/193, summarize.py:67/123 and trees.py (5 sites) default 'commons'; shim.py:35 and library.py:181 default 'library'; live.py:53 TREE = 'founding'. So 'the librarian's tree' is not a well-defined address for any probe or census, and this bug is one symptom of that. Making them agree is a refactor across five modules and wants its own ticket; fixing the constant here does not retire it.
notes: Found 2026-08-10 during the /chart survey for revision-with-receipts, whose own probe was specified to copy this one's shape. Carried to Akien as a measured finding rather than repaired in passing; he ruled the sequence: ticket it now, sail revision-with-receipts, then sail this. Deliberately NOT fixed before revision-with-receipts sails, because that ticket's validate criterion 5 uses this probe's zero-row census as its contrast measure.

chart_chain.note: The friction this ticket recorded for Akien's eye STANDS as recorded, and now with a cost attached: the seven-brick preamble ran in full for a one-constant repair. It was NOT wasted — survey is where the ticket's own MISAIMED falsifier got refuted by measurement rather than by confidence, and where the split shrank from the implied 'fix it and add a test' to a tooth-first order that buys a non-hollow demonstration for free. But that value came from ONE brick doing real work; the other six were cheap because the answer was small. Reported, not resolved: whether the bug door deserves its own shape is a spec question and Akien's.

falsifier_1_misaimed: REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-10, before any edit. Both halves of the discriminator this ticket named agree, and they agree against the ticket's own risk of pointing the wrong way. (a) The live store holds 88 rows distributed {'library': 84, 'founding': 4} — 'commons' is not a small count but an ABSENT KEY, and no row has ever existed there. (b) The four RATIFIED rows — 3 earned and 1 refuted, precisely the tenure outcomes this probe exists to watch — all sit in 'library'. (c) The charter never uses the word 'commons' at all (0 occurrences against 'library' 19, 'founding' 9), so the probe's constant was never traceable to the design. The defect is at the READING end; shim.py is correct and is not touched.

falsifier_2_insufficient.measured: 2026-08-10, at build rather than by argument. One line moved (_TREE 'commons' -> 'library') and the census returned {hypothesis: 80, earned: 3, refuted: 1}, crossings_since_landing 9, three earned nodes each spanning exactly 2 distinct corroborating questions against PROMOTION_THRESHOLD 2 — so promotion is REAL, not hollow, and the trigger's second clause has something to read. All six of the librarian's proof files green after the change. The constant was the whole defect; nothing else was severing the instrument from the corpus.
falsifier_2_insufficient.residue: Both predicates still stand down, and now for TRACEABLE reasons: 9 < _ENOUGH_CROSSINGS 20 (a young tree), and 0 rows past a 14-day DECAY_HORIZON whose oldest row is 13 days. The promotion half of _enough is already satisfied, so it is UNRIPE rather than unreachable — evaluable within about a day.

closed.proved_by: cairn/devices/librarian/proofs/test_the_probe_reads_the_tree_the_face_writes.py, sealed netns (seal measured: 1.1.1.1:53 reachable bare, unreachable inside), validation at cairn/devices/librarian/validations/test_the_probe_reads_the_tree_the_face_writes.json
closed.the_tooth_went_first: Written before the repair and RED against it (exit 1, failure text naming both ends: face 'library' / census 'commons'). The identical bytes (sha256 78ccd41230fb1162d2964d9178f37dde80d1b05977e5cb56de42a98dfda6a5ba) went green after, and the ordering was re-verified by stashing the repair and re-running the CURRENT tooth, which reds again. It reads the face's tree from inspect.signature(LibrarianShim.__init__) rather than a literal, so it reds on DISAGREEMENT — it would survive both ends moving to a third tree together, and a tooth asserting _TREE == 'library' would not.
closed.the_honest_gap: Done here is THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES, not THE TENURE LOOP IS HEALTHY. This voyage closes green with the efficacy question the probe exists to answer still open. A reader who conflates them will think the tenure loop was validated here; it was not.
for_akien: The seven-brick preamble ran for a one-constant repair. It was not wasted — survey is where falsifier (1) MISAIMED got refuted by measurement rather than by confidence, and the discriminator (which tree the RATIFIED rows occupy) is what made the fix safe. But whether a bug door should carry the full chain is still your call, and it now has one data point.

Two design questions ride forward unanswered, neither validatable here: whether the two probes should SHARE one tree name rather than each holding its own correct literal (coupling two instruments meant to be independent, against two constants that can drift apart again), and whether a probe should hold a hand-set tree constant AT ALL — blocked today by the measured absence of any single live-tree address to import (15 declaration sites, 3 distinct values, no LIVE_TREE accessor, no charter field). The second is the ticket's known_adjacent_debt and wants its own ticket.

BUILDME was journaled LATE this voyage and the record says so rather than backdating: the build ran before the crossing was recorded, because the earlier emit() was called without history_path/state_path and journaled nothing. The crossing was legal; only its timing was wrong.
